channel.title: The New Stack - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The New Stack (thenewstack.io)

item.title: Four prompt engineering patterns every developer should know — and why "draw a cat" explains them all
item.description: If your AI outputs keep missing the mark, the model probably isn't the problem — here's how to write prompts that reduce variance and get reliable results.

item.title: Minimus aims to solve one of open-source's long-festering problems
item.description: Minimus launches a free, open-source program offering hardened container images, SBOM tools, and threat intelligence to help maintainers secure their supply chains.

item.title: Exton Linux's light version will "enlighten" you
item.description: A Debian 13-based distro built around the Enlightenment desktop brings old-school Linux efficiency into the modern era — and it's fast enough to make you forget you ever left.

item.title: PwC's AI agents are now your consultants -- whether you're ready or not
item.description: PwC's new agentic platform cuts consultants out of the loop as first responders. What that means for pricing and liability remains an open question.

item.title: Kubernetes co-founder Brendan Burns: AI-generated code will become as invisible as assembly
item.description: Burns argues that as testing frameworks mature, developers will stop reviewing most code and programming languages will evolve to match.

item.title: Why programming became the proving ground for AI
item.description: Discover why software engineering's objective feedback loops make it the ideal proving ground for AI, and what other industries must learn.

item.title: Moving beyond the “magic scaling sauce” myth
item.description: Learn how to scale data-intensive applications effectively with this exclusive excerpt from Martin Kleppmann and Chris Riccomini.

item.title: There’s a hidden tax on every AI-generated merge request
item.description: AI code generation causes merge requests to surge, but human review doesn't scale. Learn how to fix the hidden tax overloading engineers.

item.title: OpenClaw vs. Hermes Agent: The race to build AI assistants that never forget
item.description: OpenClaw and Hermes Agent take different approaches to persistent AI coding assistants. One prioritizes ecosystem reach, the other deep learning over time.

item.title: Why Broadcom gave Velero to the CNCF Sandbox — and what it means for Kubernetes data protection
item.description: Broadcom donates Velero to CNCF Sandbox and extends Kubernetes support for enterprises, aiming to reduce operational overhead across cloud native infrastructure.

item.title: Why coding agents will break your CI/CD pipeline (and how to fix it)
item.description: AI coding agents are breaking CI/CD pipelines. Learn how to fix the validation bottleneck with ephemeral environments and agent skills.

item.title: The TeamPCP attacks are a warning: Your CI/CD pipeline is the new front line
item.description: TeamPCP attacks show CI/CD pipelines are the new security front line. Dan Lorenc shares how to fix flawed supply chain trust assumptions.

item.title: Why pgEdge thinks MCP (not an API) is the right way for AI agents to talk to databases
item.description: pgEdge launches a production-ready MCP Server for Postgres, bringing AI agent connectivity, schema introspection, and reduced token usage to any Postgres database.

item.title: Microsoft execs warn agentic AI is hollowing out the junior developer pipeline
item.description: Microsoft's Russinovich and Hanselman warn agentic AI's productivity gains are eliminating junior developer roles, threatening the software talent pipeline.

item.title: Anthropic's rough week: leaked models, exposed source code, and a botched GitHub takedown
item.description: Anthropic's leaked source code, exposed Claude Code architecture, and botched GitHub takedown raise questions about AI security, governance, and accountability.
